2. Petitioners predecessor-in-interest Abdul Halim instituted the aforesaid suit for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession of the suit property measuring 1.50 acre of land with building and structure thereon appertaining to Plot No.151 and 157 of Tejgaon Industrial Area, Dhaka. Briefly, the plaintiff's case is that he acquired the suit land from the then Government of East Bengal under a lease deed executed on 25-1-56 and registered on 22-3-56. The plaintiff as proprietor of Dhaka Wood Works constructed a workshop there and carried on his business. Subsequently the plaintiff and members of his family formed a private limited company in 1959 under the name of Dhaka Wood Works Ltd. The said company took a loan of Taka 1,50,000.00 from the then Pakistan Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation (PICIC) by mortgaging the suit property. On the failure of the said company to repay the loan PICIC filed Title Suit No. 315 of 1968 in the First Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for realization of Taka 1,64,952.23 by selling the properties of the plaintiffs including the suit land. The said suit was ultimately decreed on compromise and in terms of the said compromise the plaintiff was to pay a sum of Taka 90,667.00 in two equal installments, the first installment by 31st December 1970 and the second by 31st December 1971. The plaintiff paid the first installment on 12-3-70 but could not pay the second installment due to the war of liberation though he was ready to pay the same. No action was taken by the decree-holder. 

 8. While considering the main ground of defence, i.e., the bar of section 53A of the Transfer of Property Act the High Court Division found that Rana Tractors and Equipments Ltd was always ready and willing to perform their part of the contract and they paid almost the entire consideration money leaving the balance of Taka 302/90. The possession of the suit property was admittedly delivered to Rana Tractors and defendant No. 1 ultimately came to possess the same as noticed above. The defendants having been found to be in possession of the suit property and further to have satisfied all the dues under the agreement dated 29-11-1969 and the compromise decree dated 18-11-1970, the High Court Division ultimately found "that neither the deceased plaintiff nor his successors, the substituted plaintiffs, are entitled to declaration of title in the suit property and the substituted plaintiffs are debarred from asserting their title or any right in the suit property not only against the transferee Rana Tractors and Equipments Ltd but also against the defendants who have been possessing through the said purchaser company. So Court below was not justified in declaring plaintiffs title in the suit property. The deceased plaintiff having delivered possession of the suit property in part performance of written contract for sale was not entitled to recover khas possession by ejecting the defendants who are in lawful possession of the suit property. We have already found that the substituted plaintiffs have failed to prove alleged possession and dispossession."
